The Guardian — Jamie Grierson, published 27 September 2026. Found in my own lead-story audit sweep at about 07:45 BST on 28 September. Text via Exa search highlights (WebFetch refused for theguardian.com).

HEADLINE: Five arrested on terrorism charges after explosives found near RAF base used by US
STANDFIRST: Counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind suspected bomb plot after member of public calls 999 over suspicious vehicles

Counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot after armed
officers found explosives on three vans parked minutes from an RAF base used by the US military.

The Guardian understands that after five men were arrested on terrorism charges, investigators were
examining materials found in the vans, with an initial view being they were consistent with improvised
explosive devices.

[Photo caption: Five men have been arrested and three vans are being examined by army bomb disposal
experts in a possible foiled terror plot at RAF Fairford.]
